transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-04-02
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Harborlane Head of ML), Rajesh Menon (Harborlane Platform), Sofia Ruiz (Harborlane VP Product)
Shared artifacts: 'Harborlane pilot metrics spreadsheet' (link: https://drive.google.com/drive/benchmark-harborlane-0402), pilot deck (Redwood: /decks/pilot-throughput-apr02.pdf)

Summary:
Quick review of last week's steady-state run, clarified p95 SLA targets, agreed on a 350 req/s throughput target for next benchmark, discussed queue shaping and continuous batching tweaks, action items assigned for a longer-duration steady-state run and pricing follow-up. Customer reiterated need for KMS and SOC2 notes for compliance evaluation.

Topics covered:
- Steady-state results and anomalies
- Continuous batching tuning and max concurrency limits
- Queue shaping and backpressure behavior under burst
- KV cache effectiveness for prefixes and reranking flows
- Security/compliance checklist and on-prem network constraints
- Next benchmarks and timelines

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (AE): okay everyone thanks for making time, um let's do a quick status — short recap of last run and then jump into tuning. Priya, is this still the right team from Harborlane?
[00:06] Priya: yes yep this is Priya, and Rajesh and Sofia are here, thanks.
[00:09] Rajesh: morning, afternoon, yeah hi.
[00:12] Daniel (SE): hi all, I pulled up the steady state logs you sent, there's a small jitter window around minute 18 and 42 where queue depth spiked. I have notes.
[00:20] Priya: mm-hmm we saw that too, the traffic pattern had a couple of microbursts from the recommendation pipeline. We want to see how continuous batching smooths that out.
[00:27] Maya: great. For context, last week's run average batch size was 9, concurrency cap 6, we hit an average of 260 req/s, p95 was 480 ms which is above your target. What's your SLO again, Priya?
[00:37] Priya: target p95 is <= 350 ms, p50 ideally under 120 ms. For steady state we want at least 300 req/s sustained, but with bursts up to 500 req/s for short windows.
[00:47] Sofia: and the business asks that latency spikes above 1s should be rare during peak campaigns.
[00:52] Daniel: okay makes sense. A couple approaches: raise concurrency cap to 8, enable more aggressive continuous batching (we can increase max batch size to 24 but that trades off tail latency), and tune queue shaper to prioritize low-latency traffic classes.
[01:04] Rajesh: sounds good — what's the observed cost delta when going from concurrency 6 to 8? We need to understand unit economics.
[01:10] Maya: rough ballpark from our sizing calc is +18-22% GPU token cost for that pilot footprint; Daniel can provide a more precise run-based number.
[01:16] Daniel: yeah I'll quantify with the 60-minute run. Also we can try prefix KV cache for recurring contexts — that should drop token generation by ~10-15% for your rerank flow where prefix repetition is high.
[01:28] Priya: note, our reranker batch has many identical prefixes for the same session. That cache idea could be huge.
[01:33] Speaker 3: (inaudible) K V cash.. K V cache, yeah.
[01:36] Daniel: sorry, yeah KV cache — sometimes transcripts have that split.
[01:39] Priya: no worries.
[01:41] Maya: on the queue shaper side, Daniel, can you explain the shape parameters you want us to test this week?
[01:45] Daniel: sure — three knobs: concurrency cap, max batch size, and a latency bucketing policy. We'll create a policy where short requests (<150 token outputs) are in a priority queue with lower batch-slo. Longer gen requests are in a secondary queue that can tolerate slightly larger batches. Also implement a hard timeout for queue wait at 120 ms to prevent unbounded tail.
[02:02] Rajesh: how does that interact with autoscale? If we hit a 5x burst do we fallback to burst capacity or drop?
[02:06] Maya: by default pilot has burst capacity but it's bounded. We can set a policy to automatically spin up reserved nodes when queue depth exceeds threshold, or fallback to a smaller, cheaper model variant to preserve latency.
[02:17] Sofia: fallback to smaller model is fine for degrade mode as long as quality drop is acceptable. We'll need to define the quality guard rails.
[02:23] Priya: can you demonstrate the degrade path? We want to see a canary where requests switch to gpt-smallish and then back.
[02:29] Daniel: yep we can script that in the runner — it's part of the scenario. For today's tuning suggestions: increase concurrency to 8, bump max batch to 16 for the long tail queue, set the priority queue max batch to 8, enable prefix KV caching on reranker.
[02:41] Maya: good. Any concerns about memory footprint with larger batches on your end, Rajesh?
[02:45] Rajesh: our infra has a 48GB GPU instance in pilot; we don't want OOMs. What quantization are you running?
[02:50] Daniel: q8_0 is what we suggested; it fits with room to spare at batch 16 on the 48GB profile. If needed we can use q4 to squeeze more concurrency but with slight perf differences.
[02:59] Priya: can you capture GPU utilization graphs? We want to correlate utilization with latency spikes.
[03:03] Daniel: yes I'll include GPU metrics + kernel-level time breakdown.
[03:06] Maya: let's talk benchmarks — we propose a 60-minute steady-state run at 350 req/s with the new knobs, and a 10-minute burst run to 500 req/s to check backpressure and fallback logic. Daniel, you can run both and share raw logs.
[03:18] Daniel: agreed, I'll run them, export p50/p95/p99, backlog depth trace and per-request model variant history.
[03:24] Priya: timeline?
[03:25] Daniel: aiming to finish runs by 2027-04-06 and then share a single zipped artifact.
[03:29] Maya: perfect.
[03:31] [03:31] Sofia: side question re security — we need SOC2 evidence and KMS integration notes for the pilot. Do you have a SOC2 link and a short KMS integration cheat-sheet?
[03:38] Maya: yes we have SOC2 docs and a KMS integration guide; I'll send both. Our private deployment docs also include HSM/KMS patterns and VPC peering checklist.
[03:45] Rajesh: and what about log retention? Harborlane's policy is 90 days internal; do you retain token-level logs? We need to understand data residency for the pilot.
[03:53] Daniel: pilot defaults to redwood-managed logs for the hosted pilot; but for Harborlane we can enable customer-controlled retention on Dedicated or Private — you can set retention and point to your KMS. We'll call out options in the security doc.
[04:03] Priya: thanks. Also, regarding telemetry, can you emit per-route token counts so we can tie cost back to product feature?
[04:09] Maya: yes that's standard — per-route token and latency breakdown.
[04:12] Daniel: quick thing: during the minute-18 spike we saw several requests hit queue-wait of ~250 ms before batching; that was the main p95 contributor. The change to priority queue with 120 ms wait should chop that tail.
[04:23] Priya: okay good.
[04:24] [04:24] Maya: any questions about the test harness? We used the Redwood runner with the same traffic script you provided but we randomized session ids to approximate your real traffic. Any adjustments?
[04:34] Priya: the only difference is we have a small percentage of very long outputs (800-1200 tokens) for the product descriptions — you did we exclude those?
[04:40] Daniel: we didn't include those long tails in the last run; for the 60-minute run we'll inject a 5% long-output path to mimic your prod. That will give better tail behavior.
[04:49] Rajesh: and retry logic — do you preserve client retries or collapse them? We need to ensure the runner doesn't accidentally amplify traffic.
[04:55] Daniel: the runner honors original client retry patterns; we also have options to collapse retries at the gateway which you can enable. We'll document which toggle we used.
[05:03] Sofia: one more — can you estimate cost delta if we enable prefix cache? I want to present to finance.
[05:08] Maya: prefix cache reduces generation tokens by roughly 10-15% for your workload — estimate is about 8-12% cost savings on the inference token spend line, but we'll quantify it after Daniel's run.
[05:18] Priya: great.
[05:19] Speaker 2: (crosstalk) yeah yeah uh-huh.
[05:22] Maya: ok recap of decisions: concurrency cap -> 8, priority queue with max batch 8 and 120 ms wait, long queue max batch 16, prefix KV cache enabled for reranker, include 5% long outputs in test, run steady-state 60m @ 350 req/s and 10m spike to 500 req/s.
[05:38] Daniel: I'll attach the run config and runner script to the artifact.
[05:41] Maya: actions and owners recorded. Anything else on security?
[05:45] Priya: please send SOC2 link and KMS guide, we need that before the exec review next week.
[05:50] Maya: will do by tomorrow.
[05:52] Sofia: also schedule the on-prem/net sync — Rajesh will coordinate with you, Daniel.
[05:59] Rajesh: I'll send availabilities.
[06:02] Daniel: quick note on fallback: we can implement transparent model fallback plus a small A/B on quality for the same request id so product can inspect the delta. That will help validating degrade mode.
[06:12] Priya: nice.
[06:13] Maya: ok let's close with next steps and timelines — Daniel runs by 2027-04-06, Maya sends pricing and SOC2/KMS notes by 2027-04-03, Priya uploads traffic sample by 2027-04-05, schedule on-prem sync week of 2027-04-12.
[06:27] Sofia: thanks all, that works for us.
[06:29] Maya: thanks, we'll follow up in email with the artifact links. Bye.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional label swaps and muffled audio around minute marks; speaker 3 label used once. Some technical terms transcribed with spacing errors (K V cache).
